definitions.gloss: to reduce, to decrease, to diminish
definitions.explanation: To make something smaller in amount, degree, or intensity. A formal or written-style verb used in official, academic, and journalistic contexts. Can be used both transitively (to reduce something) and intransitively (for something to decrease).

examples.japanese: {刑|けい}を{減|げん}じる{措置|そち}がとられた。
examples.english: Measures were taken to reduce the sentence.

examples.japanese: {税金|ぜいきん}を{一割|いちわり}{減|げん}じることが{決定|けってい}された。
examples.english: It was decided to reduce taxes by ten percent.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal, written-style verb. In everyday conversation, {減|へ}らす (transitive) or {減|へ}る (intransitive) are far more common. {減|げん}じる appears in legal, administrative, and academic writing.

The variant {減|げん}ずる (classical conjugation) is also used and carries an even more formal tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {刑|けい}を{減|げん}じる: to reduce a sentence
- {税|ぜい}を{減|げん}じる: to reduce taxes
- {経費|けいひ}を{減|げん}じる: to reduce expenses
- {負担|ふたん}を{減|げん}じる: to reduce a burden

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {減|へ}らす: to reduce (everyday transitive)
- {減|へ}る: to decrease (everyday intransitive)
- {減少|げんしょう}する: to decrease (formal, noun + suru)
